ut-kufta-bozbash: Cover the bone-in lamb with cold water, bring it up and skim. Add the chickpeas and simmer for an hour.
Work a grated onion, the rice, salt and pepper into the mince and knead for five minutes, until the mass pulls back at your hand.
Divide the mince into four. Hide a plum and an apricot in each and shape a tight ball with no cracks.
Lower the kufta into the barely simmering broth and cook thirty minutes without stirring. For the first five minutes do not touch it at all.
Add the potatoes whole and the turmeric and cook twenty minutes more, until the potatoes are tender.
Into each bowl goes one kufta, one potato and some chickpeas; ladle over the broth and crumble dried mint on top.
ut-beshbarmak: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim, and simmer on the lowest heat for two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into squares of about eight centimetres.
Slice the onion into rings, pour a ladle of hot broth over it and leave it ten minutes; this is the sorpa that dresses the dish.
Lift out the meat, skim the fat into a separate bowl and boil the dough squares in that broth in batches, three to four minutes each.
Pull the meat apart into thin sheets across the grain. Lay the dough on a large platter, the meat on top, the onions and their broth over that.
Serve the remaining broth hot in bowls with herbs; it is drunk before the dish or alongside it.
ut-beshbarmak-gf: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim, and simmer on the lowest heat for two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into squares of about eight centimetres.
Slice the onion into rings, pour a ladle of hot broth over it and leave it ten minutes; this is the sorpa that dresses the dish.
Lift out the meat, skim the fat into a separate bowl and boil the dough squares in that broth in batches, three to four minutes each.
Pull the meat apart into thin sheets across the grain. Lay the dough on a large platter, the meat on top, the onions and their broth over that.
Serve the remaining broth hot in bowls with herbs; it is drunk before the dish or alongside it.
ut-baursaki: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Work in the eggs, melted butter, salt and flour to a soft dough. It should stay slightly tacky.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for an hour, until the dough has doubled.
Knock it back, roll it out a centimetre and a half thick and cut it into three-centimetre squares or diamonds.
Let the pieces stand under a cloth for twenty minutes; this second rise is the reason for the hollow.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry in batches for two to three minutes, turning, to an even gold.
Drain on paper and serve warm, with tea, soured cream or honey.
ut-bryndzove-halusky: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly; only a little water should go, as a dry mass will not bind.
Mix in the flour, egg and salt. The mass should slide off a spoon slowly rather than pour.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Push the dough into boiling salted water through a colander with large holes. The dumplings are done when they float, after about three minutes.
Drain the dumplings, return them to the warm pan and stir in the brynza with a spoon of the cooking water. Keep the heat off.
Serve into bowls, spoon over the hot fat and scatter the crackling on top.
ut-bryndzove-halusky-gf: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly; only a little water should go, as a dry mass will not bind.
Mix in the gluten-free flour, egg and salt. The mass should slide off a spoon slowly rather than pour.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Push the dough into boiling salted water through a colander with large holes. The dumplings are done when they float, after about three minutes.
Drain the dumplings, return them to the warm pan and stir in the brynza with a spoon of the cooking water. Keep the heat off.
Serve into bowls, spoon over the hot fat and scatter the crackling on top.
ut-kapustnica: Soak the mushrooms in a cup of warm water for twenty minutes. Keep the water.
Simmer the smoked ribs in two litres of water for forty minutes with the bay.
Squeeze the kraut and set the brine aside. Add the kraut, the mushrooms with their water and the prunes to the broth and cook thirty minutes.
Fry the onion, take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and flour and let it down with a ladle of broth until smooth.
Pour the roux into the pot, add the sausage and cook fifteen minutes more.
Strip the meat off the bones, return it to the soup and bring the sourness up with the brine to taste. Serve with soured cream.
ut-kapustnica-gf: Soak the mushrooms in a cup of warm water for twenty minutes. Keep the water.
Simmer the smoked ribs in two litres of water for forty minutes with the bay.
Squeeze the kraut and set the brine aside. Add the kraut, the mushrooms with their water and the prunes to the broth and cook thirty minutes.
Fry the onion, take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and gluten-free flour and let it down with a ladle of broth until smooth.
Pour the roux into the pot, add the sausage and cook fifteen minutes more.
Strip the meat off the bones, return it to the soup and bring the sourness up with the brine to taste. Serve with soured cream.
ut-pastel-de-choclo: Fry the finely chopped onion until translucent, add the mince, cumin, salt and pepper and cook through. Let the pino cool; warm, it will weep.
Blitz the corn with the basil and milk to a coarse but even mass.
Cook it down with the butter over medium heat, stirring, for about fifteen minutes, until a spoon stands up in it.
Divide the pino between earthenware dishes and top each with a piece of chicken, half an egg and a couple of olives with raisins.
Cover with a two-centimetre layer of the corn mass, level it and dust with sugar.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, the last five under the grill, to a dark caramel crust.
ut-empanadas-de-pino: Dice the onion and sweat it in fat for twenty minutes over a low heat; it should turn sweet, not brown.
Add the meat, paprika and cumin and stew twenty minutes. By volume there should be at least as much onion as meat.
Chill the filling for at least three hours, ideally overnight.
Knead a dough from the flour, melted fat, warm milk and salt. Work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Roll out twenty-centimetre rounds. On each go two spoons of filling, an olive, a quarter egg and a pinch of raisins.
Fold into a parcel, seal the edges and turn them over twice. Prick the top with a toothpick so steam can escape.
Brush with yolk and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep gold.
ut-empanadas-de-pino-gf: Dice the onion and sweat it in fat for twenty minutes over a low heat; it should turn sweet, not brown.
Add the meat, paprika and cumin and stew twenty minutes. By volume there should be at least as much onion as meat.
Chill the filling for at least three hours, ideally overnight.
Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, melted fat, warm milk and salt. Work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Roll out twenty-centimetre rounds. On each go two spoons of filling, an olive, a quarter egg and a pinch of raisins.
Fold into a parcel, seal the edges and turn them over twice. Prick the top with a toothpick so steam can escape.
Brush with yolk and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep gold.
ut-pabellon-criollo: Boil the beans with half the onion and some garlic until soft, an hour to ninety minutes. Salt at the end.
Simmer the beef whole in salted water for an hour and twenty minutes. Lift it out and cool it enough to handle.
Pull the meat into threads along the grain. Across the grain it shreds into crumbs.
Fry the remaining onion, pepper and garlic, add the tomatoes and cumin, then the meat, and stew twenty minutes with a ladle of the broth.
Cook the rice loose, without butter or spice; here it is the neutral part.
Slice the plantain on the diagonal and fry over medium heat until caramel on both sides.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, meat and plantain side by side, unmixed.
ut-cachapas: Cut the kernels from the cobs and blend them with the milk, sugar and salt to a coarse but pourable purée.
Let the batter stand ten minutes. The starch swells and the pancakes hold together.
Heat a pan to medium, butter it and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it into a circle a centimetre thick.
Cook four minutes, until the edges dry and the underside is mottled, flip and give it three more.
Lay butter and cheese on the hot cachapa, fold it over and press it with a spatula.
Serve at once. A cooled cachapa loses its softness and turns into a dense cake.
ut-saltenas: Fry the onion with the ají and cumin, add the beef and cook through. Pour in the stock and simmer ten minutes.
Dissolve the gelatine in a couple of spoons of hot water and stir it into the stew with the potato and peas.
Cool the filling and refrigerate it for at least four hours; it has to set to a firm jelly.
Knead a dough from the flour, softened butter, sugar, achiote, salt and warm water. Rest it half an hour.
Roll fifteen-centimetre rounds. On each go a spoon of the cold jelly, a wedge of egg and an olive.
Seal the seam in a plait along the top and stand the pastries seam-up. Any gap means the broth escapes.
Bake at 220 °C for twenty-five minutes. The high heat is what sets the pastry before the jelly melts.
ut-saltenas-gf: Fry the onion with the ají and cumin, add the beef and cook through. Pour in the stock and simmer ten minutes.
Dissolve the gelatine in a couple of spoons of hot water and stir it into the stew with the potato and peas.
Cool the filling and refrigerate it for at least four hours; it has to set to a firm jelly.
Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, softened butter, sugar, achiote, salt and warm water. Rest it half an hour.
Roll fifteen-centimetre rounds. On each go a spoon of the cold jelly, a wedge of egg and an olive.
Seal the seam in a plait along the top and stand the pastries seam-up. Any gap means the broth escapes.
Bake at 220 °C for twenty-five minutes. The high heat is what sets the pastry before the jelly melts.
ut-silpancho: Pound the meat under film to three or four millimetres. Work from the centre outwards or it tears.
Season and press into breadcrumbs with the flat of your hand. No egg wash is used here.
Dice the tomato, onion and beetroot small, mix with the parsley, salt and a spoon of oil.
Fry the boiled potato slices until golden and keep them warm.
Fry the steaks a minute and a half a side in hot oil; meat this thin cooks instantly.
Fry the eggs, leaving the yolks runny.
Build it: rice, potato, the steak across the whole plate, the egg, and the raw salsa over the top.
ut-silpancho-gf: Pound the meat under film to three or four millimetres. Work from the centre outwards or it tears.
Season and press into gluten-free breadcrumbs with the flat of your hand. No egg wash is used here.
Dice the tomato, onion and beetroot small, mix with the parsley, salt and a spoon of oil.
Fry the boiled potato slices until golden and keep them warm.
Fry the steaks a minute and a half a side in hot oil; meat this thin cooks instantly.
Fry the eggs, leaving the yolks runny.
Build it: rice, potato, the steak across the whole plate, the egg, and the raw salsa over the top.
ut-encebollado: Cure the onion in the juice of two limes with salt and leave it at least fifteen minutes.
Fry the garlic and tomatoes with the cumin for five minutes, add a litre and a half of water and bring it up.
Lower in the tuna whole and poach it fifteen minutes on a low heat. Fish does not tolerate a hard boil.
Lift out the fish, strain the broth and return it to the heat. Cook the cassava in it for twenty minutes, until soft.
Flake the tuna coarsely, discarding the dark parts, and return it to the pot for two minutes.
Ladle it out and top with the cured onion and its juice and coriander. Serve with a wedge of lime.
ut-llapingachos: Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel them hot and mash them dry. Add no liquid at all.
Warm the achiote in a spoon of oil for a minute and work the coloured oil into the mash with salt.
Roll balls, press a cube of cheese into each, close them up and flatten into cakes a centimetre thick.
Chill the cakes for half an hour; that is what holds their shape in the pan.
For the sauce fry the onion, add the peanut butter and milk and simmer five minutes to the thickness of cream.
Fry the cakes over medium heat, four minutes a side, to a golden crust.
Serve with a fried egg, the sauce and an avocado salad.
ut-llapingachos-nf: Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel them hot and mash them dry. Add no liquid at all.
Warm the achiote in a spoon of oil for a minute and work the coloured oil into the mash with salt.
Roll balls, press a cube of cheese into each, close them up and flatten into cakes a centimetre thick.
Chill the cakes for half an hour; that is what holds their shape in the pan.
For the sauce fry the onion, add the sunflower seed butter and milk and simmer five minutes to the thickness of cream.
Fry the cakes over medium heat, four minutes a side, to a golden crust.
Serve with a fried egg, the sauce and an avocado salad.
ut-masgouf: Cut the fish along the back without separating the belly, gut it and open it out like a book. Leave the spine in.
Mix the oil, turmeric, tamarind, curry powder, salt and pepper and paint the flesh with it. Leave the skin alone.
Leave the fish half an hour at room temperature; cold, it cooks unevenly.
Light the fire and let it settle to a steady flame. Stand the fish upright, flesh towards the fire, half a metre away.
Cook for an hour, turning as needed. The flesh should whiten and dry at the edges without scorching.
Move the fish skin down onto the coals, lay the onion and tomato over it and give it ten more minutes.
Serve it on the board, with gluten-free flatbread, lemon and raw onion.
ut-dolma-iraqi: Rinse the rice and mix it with the mince, chopped parsley, tomato paste, baharat, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut lids off the peppers and tomatoes and hollow them. Blanch the onions whole and separate them into layers.
Roll the filling in vine leaves into tight cylinders — the rice doubles, so leave it room.
Fill the vegetables two-thirds full and put their lids back on.
Line the pot with tomato slices, then layer the parcels and stuffed vegetables, the heaviest at the bottom.
Mix water with the pomegranate molasses, lemon juice and salt and pour it in until it reaches the top layer.
Cover with a weighted plate and cook on a low heat for an hour and fifteen minutes. Serve by inverting the pot onto a platter.
ut-mansaf: Soak the jameed in warm water for four hours, break it up by hand and pass it through a sieve to an even liquid.
Simmer the lamb with the cardamom for an hour and twenty minutes, skimming. Keep the broth.
Pour the jameed liquid in with the meat and bring it up, stirring continuously in one direction.
Drop the heat to its lowest and hold it forty minutes. The sauce thickens and turns creamy.
Cook the rice in the meat broth with turmeric and a spoon of ghee.
Fry the almonds and pine nuts in ghee until golden and set them aside.
Line a platter with the bread, moisten it with sauce, spread the rice, lay the meat on top, spoon over more sauce and scatter the nuts and parsley.
ut-maqluba: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cinnamon and baharat for forty minutes. Lift out the meat and strain the broth.
Soak the rice in warm water for twenty minutes and rinse until the water runs clear.
Slice the aubergines into rounds, salt them and leave fifteen minutes, then pat dry and fry until browned.
Fry the cauliflower florets and potato slices until golden and drain them on paper.
Lay the potato on the bottom of the pot, aubergine up the sides, then chicken, cauliflower and rice on top. Do not press it down.
Pour in hot broth to a finger above the rice, bring it up and cook covered on a low heat for forty minutes.
Take it off the heat, rest it ten minutes, cover with a platter and invert in one movement. Scatter with pine nuts.
ut-maqluba-nf: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cinnamon and baharat for forty minutes. Lift out the meat and strain the broth.
Soak the rice in warm water for twenty minutes and rinse until the water runs clear.
Slice the aubergines into rounds, salt them and leave fifteen minutes, then pat dry and fry until browned.
Fry the cauliflower florets and potato slices until golden and drain them on paper.
Lay the potato on the bottom of the pot, aubergine up the sides, then chicken, cauliflower and rice on top. Do not press it down.
Pour in hot broth to a finger above the rice, bring it up and cook covered on a low heat for forty minutes.
Take it off the heat, rest it ten minutes, cover with a platter and invert in one movement. Scatter with sunflower seeds.
ut-brik: Mix the mashed potato with the tuna, chopped onion, capers, parsley, harissa, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Test with a scrap of pastry: it should surface at once and sizzle.
Lay a sheet on a plate, put two spoons of filling on one half and make a hollow in it.
Break an egg into the hollow, season it and fold the sheet over immediately, pressing the edges.
Slide the brik into the oil and fry forty seconds a side, steadying it with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
ut-shakshuka-tunisienne: Boil the chickpeas in two litres of water with half the garlic for ninety minutes, until soft but whole.
Pound the remaining garlic with salt and cumin to a paste and stir it into the broth. Season.
Soft-boil the eggs, six minutes from the boil, and peel them.
Tear the bread into large pieces into deep bowls, filling them halfway.
Ladle the hot broth and chickpeas over the bread until it is thoroughly soaked.
Top with an egg, a spoon of harissa, olives, capers and tuna, then olive oil and lemon.
ut-shakshuka-tunisienne-gf: Boil the chickpeas in two litres of water with half the garlic for ninety minutes, until soft but whole.
Pound the remaining garlic with salt and cumin to a paste and stir it into the broth. Season.
Soft-boil the eggs, six minutes from the boil, and peel them.
Tear the gluten-free bread into large pieces into deep bowls, filling them halfway.
Ladle the hot broth and chickpeas over the gluten-free bread until it is thoroughly soaked.
Top with an egg, a spoon of harissa, olives, capers and tuna, then olive oil and lemon.
ut-couscous-algerien: Brown the meat with the onion in the base of the couscoussier, add the tomato paste, spices and chickpeas and cover with water. Cook an hour.
Sprinkle the couscous with water and oil and rub it between your hands so the grains separate. Steam it fifteen minutes.
Turn the grain into a wide dish, sprinkle again, rake it apart and let it cool five minutes.
Return it to the steam for fifteen more minutes. Meanwhile add the carrot and turnip to the broth.
Rake it a third time, working in the butter, and steam it a final ten minutes.
Add the courgette and pumpkin to the broth for the last twenty minutes; they cook faster than the roots.
Mound the couscous, meat and vegetables on top. Serve the broth in a separate bowl and the harissa in a third.
ut-couscous-algerien-gf: Brown the meat with the onion in the base of the couscoussier, add the tomato paste, spices and chickpeas and cover with water. Cook an hour.
Sprinkle the quinoa with water and oil and rub it between your hands so the grains separate. Steam it fifteen minutes.
Turn the grain into a wide dish, sprinkle again, rake it apart and let it cool five minutes.
Return it to the steam for fifteen more minutes. Meanwhile add the carrot and turnip to the broth.
Rake it a third time, working in the butter, and steam it a final ten minutes.
Add the courgette and pumpkin to the broth for the last twenty minutes; they cook faster than the roots.
Mound the quinoa, meat and vegetables on top. Serve the broth in a separate bowl and the harissa in a third.
ut-chorba-frik: Brown the meat with the onion and celery in ghee for ten minutes.
Add the grated tomato, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook five minutes.
Pour in two litres of boiling water, add the chickpeas and simmer forty minutes.
Rinse the freekeh, add it and cook twenty minutes more, stirring; the grain settles and catches.
Stir in the coriander five minutes before the end and loosen with water if the soup has gone too thick.
Ladle out, crumble dried mint over each bowl and add lemon juice.
ut-chorba-frik-gf: Brown the meat with the onion and celery in ghee for ten minutes.
Add the grated tomato, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook five minutes.
Pour in two litres of boiling water, add the chickpeas and simmer forty minutes.
Rinse the brown rice, add it and cook twenty minutes more, stirring; the grain settles and catches.
Stir in the coriander five minutes before the end and loosen with water if the soup has gone too thick.
Ladle out, crumble dried mint over each bowl and add lemon juice.
ut-cepelinai: Grate the raw potato finely and wring it out in a cloth. Collect the liquid in a bowl.
Let the liquid stand ten minutes, pour off the water and stir the settled starch back into the grated potato.
Mash the boiled potato and combine it with the grated, adding the starch and salt. The mass should shape without sticking.
Mix the mince with half the finely chopped onion, marjoram, salt and pepper and roll four firm balls.
With wet hands take a lump of dough, flatten it on your palm, set the filling in it and seal it into an elongated oval.
Lower them into barely simmering salted water and cook twenty-five minutes. Do not stir; just rock the pot once in the first minute.
Render the pork fat with the remaining onion to crackling, spoon it over the cepelinai and serve with soured cream.
ut-saltibarsciai: Boil the beetroot until tender, cool it completely and grate it coarsely.
Cut the cucumbers into matchsticks and chop the dill and spring onion.
Mix the beetroot, cucumber and herbs with the soured cream and salt it now, before the kefir, so the salt disperses.
Pour in the cold kefir and stir. The soup turns an even pink.
Chill it for an hour. Warm šaltibarščiai makes no sense.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot on a separate plate. Put halved eggs into the soup.
ut-pelekie-zirni-ar-speki: Soak the peas twelve hours in cold water, changing it once.
Drain, cover with fresh water two fingers above and boil unsalted for an hour and twenty minutes, until soft.
Dice the pork belly and render it in a dry pan to golden crackling.
Add the chopped onion and fry it in the rendered fat until soft and golden.
Drain the peas, leaving a little liquid in the pot, and season with salt and pepper.
Stir the crackling, onion and fat into the peas and serve hot, with cold kefir in a glass.
ut-rupjmaizes-kartojums: Crumb the stale bread in a blender or by hand to a coarse crumb.
Mix the crumbs with the sugar and cinnamon and dry them in the oven at 160 °C for twelve minutes, stirring twice.
Cool the crumbs completely. On warm crumbs the cream collapses and the layers merge.
Whip the cold cream with the vanilla sugar to firm peaks.
Layer into glasses: crumbs, jam, cream, and repeat. Finish with cream.
Chill for at least four hours, ideally overnight. Serve with cranberries on top.
ut-mulgipuder: Rinse the barley and boil it in salted water for an hour, until soft.
Add the roughly cut potato to the same pot and cook twenty minutes more.
Render the pork belly to crackling, add the onion and fry until golden.
Drain most of the water from the barley and potato, keeping half a cup.
Mash with the butter and milk, leaving the barley grains still visible. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve into bowls and spoon the crackling, onion and rendered fat over the top.
ut-mulgipuder-gf: Rinse the brown rice and boil it in salted water for an hour, until soft.
Add the roughly cut potato to the same pot and cook twenty minutes more.
Render the pork belly to crackling, add the onion and fry until golden.
Drain most of the water from the brown rice and potato, keeping half a cup.
Mash with the butter and milk, leaving the brown rice grains still visible. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve into bowls and spoon the crackling, onion and rendered fat over the top.
ut-kama: Whisk the kefir with the sugar and a pinch of salt until the sugar has dissolved.
Add the kama a little at a time, whisking; all at once it lumps, and the lumps never break up.
Leave it fifteen minutes for the gluten-free flour to swell, then check the consistency and let it down with more kefir if needed.
Stir in the honey and divide between glasses.
Chill for an hour and serve with berries and, if you like, a spoon of whipped cream.
ut-draniki: Grate the potato and onion finely into the same bowl.
Let the mass stand three minutes and pour off the water that gathers on top, leaving the sediment.
Season with salt and pepper. Add nothing else.
Heat the oil over medium and drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattening it to half a centimetre.
Fry three to four minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with soured cream and dill.
ut-machanka: Brown the pork well, add the onion and fry until soft.
Add the sliced sausage and ribs, pour in a cup of water, add the bay and stew twenty-five minutes.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Simmer ten minutes on a low heat, until the gravy thickens to the consistency of pouring cream.
Whisk a pancake batter from the flour, milk, eggs and salt and let it stand fifteen minutes.
Cook thin unsweetened pancakes in a dry pan.
Serve the machanka in a deep bowl with the pancakes stacked beside it. You tear off a piece and dip.
ut-machanka-gf: Brown the pork well, add the onion and fry until soft.
Add the sliced sausage and ribs, pour in a cup of water, add the bay and stew twenty-five minutes.
Whisk the gluten-free gluten-free flour into the soured cream until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Simmer ten minutes on a low heat, until the gravy thickens to the consistency of pouring cream.
Whisk a pancake batter from the gluten-free gluten-free flour, milk, eggs and salt and let it stand fifteen minutes.
Cook thin unsweetened pancakes in a dry pan.
Serve the machanka in a deep bowl with the pancakes stacked beside it. You tear off a piece and dip.
ut-mohinga: Poach the fish with the lemongrass and turmeric for fifteen minutes, lift it out and pick the flesh, discarding bones and skin. Strain the broth.
Pound the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry it in oil with the paprika until dark and fragrant.
Mash the fish with a fork and stir it into the paste, frying five minutes; it should break down into threads.
Transfer everything to the pot with the broth, add the fish sauce and simmer twenty minutes.
Slake the rice and chickpea flours in cold water to a thin slurry and pour it into the soup in a stream, stirring.
Cook twenty minutes more, until the broth thickens to the consistency of thin cream.
Boil the noodles, divide them between bowls, ladle the soup over and serve with egg, split peas, coriander and lime.
ut-lahpet-thoke: Fry the garlic slices in oil until golden and lift them out at once; a few seconds more and they turn bitter.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan until fragrant, two minutes, stirring.
Rinse the tea paste in cold water if it is very salty and squeeze it dry.
Shred the cabbage fine, cut the tomatoes into wedges and the chilli into rings.
Combine everything in a bowl with the peanuts, beans, sesame, garlic oil, fish sauce and lime juice.
Toss it with your hands immediately before serving and scatter the fried garlic over the top.
ut-lahpet-thoke-nf: Fry the garlic slices in oil until golden and lift them out at once; a few seconds more and they turn bitter.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan until fragrant, two minutes, stirring.
Rinse the tea paste in cold water if it is very salty and squeeze it dry.
Shred the cabbage fine, cut the tomatoes into wedges and the chilli into rings.
Combine everything in a bowl with the toasted sunflower seeds, beans, sesame, garlic oil, fish sauce and lime juice.
Toss it with your hands immediately before serving and scatter the fried garlic over the top.
ut-fish-amok: Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, shallot and half the lime leaves in a mortar to a smooth paste.
Warm the paste in a pan with half the coconut milk for five minutes, until it smells right.
Take it off the heat, cool it to warm and whisk in the eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar and the rest of the milk.
Fold the fish pieces through and leave them to marinate fifteen minutes.
Fold cups from the banana leaves, or use ramekins. Line the bottom with spinach leaves.
Divide the fish and sauce between them without filling to the brim and steam for twenty minutes.
Spoon over the coconut cream, scatter with shredded lime leaves and serve with rice.
ut-lok-lak: Marinate the beef in the oyster and soy sauces with garlic, sugar and half the pepper for twenty minutes.
Mix the lime juice with the remaining pepper and a pinch of salt; that is the dipping sauce.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and cucumber slices and red onion rings on a platter.
Heat a pan as high as it goes and sear the beef in batches, a minute and a half each, without stirring constantly.
Fry the eggs, keeping the yolks runny.
Pile the beef on the vegetables, top with the eggs and give everyone their own small bowl of the dip.
ut-lok-lak-gf: Marinate the beef in the oyster and tamari with garlic, sugar and half the pepper for twenty minutes.
Mix the lime juice with the remaining pepper and a pinch of salt; that is the dipping sauce.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and cucumber slices and red onion rings on a platter.
Heat a pan as high as it goes and sear the beef in batches, a minute and a half each, without stirring constantly.
Fry the eggs, keeping the yolks runny.
Pile the beef on the vegetables, top with the eggs and give everyone their own small bowl of the dip.
ut-hainanese-chicken-rice: Rub the chicken with salt inside and out and stuff the cavity with half the ginger and the spring onions.
Bring a pot of water to the boil, lower the whole chicken in, bring it back up and turn the heat off immediately.
Keep it covered for forty minutes without lifting the lid. It is done when the juices from the thigh run clear.
Move the chicken into iced water for ten minutes, then pat it dry and brush it with sesame oil.
Skim the fat from the broth, fry the chopped garlic and ginger in it, add the rinsed rice and toast it three minutes.
Add broth to the rice at one and a half to one, drop in the pandan leaf and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Pound the chillies with garlic, ginger and lime into a sauce. Joint the chicken and serve with the rice, cucumber, sauce and a bowl of the broth.
ut-hainanese-chicken-rice-gf: Rub the chicken with salt inside and out and stuff the cavity with half the ginger and the spring onions.
Bring a pot of water to the boil, lower the whole chicken in, bring it back up and turn the heat off immediately.
Keep it covered for forty minutes without lifting the lid. It is done when the juices from the thigh run clear.
Move the chicken into iced water for ten minutes, then pat it dry and brush it with sesame oil.
Skim the fat from the broth, fry the chopped garlic and ginger in it, add the rinsed rice and toast it three minutes.
Add broth to the rice at one and a half to one, drop in the pandan leaf and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Pound the chillies with garlic, ginger and lime into a sauce. Joint the chicken and serve with the rice, cucumber, sauce and a bowl of the broth.
ut-chilli-crab: Joint the crab: lift the shell, cut the body into four and crack the claws with the back of a knife.
Pound the garlic, ginger and chillies to a paste and fry it in oil for three minutes, until fragrant.
Add the sambal, ketchup, sugar and vinegar and cook two minutes, until the sauce darkens.
Pour in the stock, bring it up and add the crab pieces. Cover and cook eight minutes.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.
Turn off the heat and pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream, stirring once in a circle.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the fried mantou.
ut-lu-rou-fan: Dice the belly into one-centimetre cubes, keeping the fat with the meat.
Fry the sliced shallots in oil to a deep golden crisp and set half aside for serving.
In the same oil brown the pork, rendering some of its fat, for ten minutes.
Add the wine, let it cook off for a minute, then add both soy sauces, the sugar, spices and garlic.
Add water level with the meat, bring it up and braise covered for ninety minutes on the lowest heat.
Add the boiled eggs to the sauce for the last twenty minutes; they take on the colour and flavour.
Serve over rice with half an egg, blanched greens and the fried shallots on top.
ut-lu-rou-fan-gf: Dice the belly into one-centimetre cubes, keeping the fat with the meat.
Fry the sliced shallots in oil to a deep golden crisp and set half aside for serving.
In the same oil brown the pork, rendering some of its fat, for ten minutes.
Add the wine, let it cook off for a minute, then add the tamari, the sugar, spices and garlic.
Add water level with the meat, bring it up and braise covered for ninety minutes on the lowest heat.
Add the boiled eggs to the sauce for the last twenty minutes; they take on the colour and flavour.
Serve over rice with half an egg, blanched greens and the fried shallots on top.
ut-beef-noodle-soup-taiwan: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, boil two minutes and drain; this removes the scum.
Fry the ginger, garlic and doubanjiang in oil for five minutes, until the oil turns red.
Add the tomatoes, wine and soy sauce, cook three minutes and return the meat to the pot.
Add water two fingers above the meat, drop in the star anise, cinnamon and sugar and simmer two hours.
Lift out the meat, cut it into thick slices and return it to the broth for ten minutes.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot of clean water and blanch the bok choy.
Divide the noodles between bowls, add the meat and greens, ladle over the broth and top with pickled mustard greens and spring onion.
ut-nyama-choma: Rub the meat with salt, pepper, the juice of two lemons, crushed garlic and oil. Leave it an hour.
Light the coals and let them ash over. The heat is right when you can hold a palm above the grate for five seconds.
Lay the meat on in whole pieces and grill, turning every ten minutes, for an hour and twenty.
Mix the diced tomato, onion, coriander and chilli with lemon juice and salt; that is kachumbari.
For the ugali bring a litre of water to the boil, rain in the gluten-free flour, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, and work it fifteen minutes into a firm mass.
Rest the meat ten minutes, cut it small across the grain and serve with ugali, kachumbari and salt.
ut-sukuma-wiki: Strip the tough stems from the leaves, roll the leaves up and shred them fine.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the garlic and cumin and warm them a minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they collapse into a paste.
Add the greens, salt them and stir. They collapse by half within a minute.
Add half a cup of water, cover and stew ten minutes; the greens should soften but stay green.
Finish with lemon juice and serve with ugali or rice.
ut-waakye: Rinse the sorghum leaves and boil them in a litre and a half of water for ten minutes; the water turns deep red.
Take the leaves out, add a pinch of soda and the beans and cook forty-five minutes, until nearly done.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot. The liquid should stand a finger above the rice.
Salt it, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without stirring.
Take it off the heat, leave it covered ten minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Fry slices of ripe plantain until caramel-coloured.
Serve with egg, gari, shito and plantain, all on one plate.
ut-banku-with-tilapia: Mix the maize and cassava doughs with a litre of water and salt to a smooth, lump-free batter.
Set it over medium heat and work it with a wooden paddle without stopping. It starts to thicken after five minutes.
Keep working it for twenty minutes, pressing it against the sides, until it turns dense and glossy.
Shape balls with wet hands and wrap each in film or a banana leaf.
Rub the fish with salt, ginger and garlic and grill or pan-fry it eight minutes a side.
Grind the tomatoes, habaneros, onion, salt and a spoon of oil in a mortar to a coarse sauce.
Serve a ball of banku, the fish and a bowl of sauce. It is eaten by hand, pinching off dough and dipping it.
ut-thieboudienne: Pound the parsley, garlic, chilli and salt into the rof paste and press it into slashes cut in the fish.
Fry the fish three minutes a side and set it aside.
In the same oil fry the onion until soft, add the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add two litres of water, the tamarind and the vegetables and cook twenty-five minutes.
Return the fish to the pot for ten minutes, then lift it and the vegetables out and keep them warm.
Add the rinsed rice to the remaining broth — twice as much liquid as rice — and cook covered for thirty minutes without stirring.
Turn the rice onto a large platter with the fish and vegetables on top. Share out the caught layer from the bottom separately.
ut-yassa-poulet: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper, pour it over the chicken and onions and chill for at least four hours.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and brown it in oil on all sides.
In the same pan cook the onion from the marinade over medium heat for twenty-five minutes, until golden and soft.
Pour in the remaining marinade and the stock and add the bay leaves and the whole chilli.
Return the chicken, cover and stew thirty minutes on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce ten minutes more until thick. Remove the chilli.
Serve with boiled rice, the onions piled over the chicken.
ut-bobotie: Soak the bread in half the milk for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the curry powder and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the mince and cook, breaking up lumps, until it loses its pink, about ten minutes.
Stir in the bread, apricots, raisins, chutney, vinegar, salt and pepper and take it off the heat.
Press it into a dish, level it and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk, pour it over, stand the bay leaves in the custard and scatter the almonds.
Return it to the oven for twenty minutes, until the custard sets and turns golden.
ut-bobotie-gfnf: Soak the gluten-free bread in half the milk for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the curry powder and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the mince and cook, breaking up lumps, until it loses its pink, about ten minutes.
Stir in the gluten-free bread, apricots, raisins, chutney, vinegar, salt and pepper and take it off the heat.
Press it into a dish, level it and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk, pour it over, stand the bay leaves in the custard and scatter the sunflower seeds.
Return it to the oven for twenty minutes, until the custard sets and turns golden.
ut-chakalaka: Grate the carrots coarsely and cut the peppers and onions into thin strips.
Fry the onion with the garlic, ginger and chilli in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the curry powder and paprika and warm them a minute; the spices need to open up in the oil.
Add the peppers and carrot and cook five minutes over a high heat, stirring.
Add the tomatoes, season and cook seven minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the beans, warm them three minutes and take the pan off. The vegetables should still have bite.
ut-plokkfiskur: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, peel them and cut them into large pieces.
Poach the cod in salted water for eight minutes, lift it out and flake it by hand, removing bones and skin.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, stirring.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking continuously, and bring the sauce to the thickness of cream.
Stir in the mustard, salt and pepper, add the fish and potato and warm everything through for five minutes.
Mash with a fork to a coarse, uneven texture in which the pieces are still recognisable, and scatter with chives.
ut-plokkfiskur-gf: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, peel them and cut them into large pieces.
Poach the cod in salted water for eight minutes, lift it out and flake it by hand, removing bones and skin.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook it two minutes, stirring.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking continuously, and bring the sauce to the thickness of cream.
Stir in the mustard, salt and pepper, add the fish and potato and warm everything through for five minutes.
Mash with a fork to a coarse, uneven texture in which the pieces are still recognisable, and scatter with chives.
ut-kjotsupa: Cover the meat with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim carefully.
Simmer for an hour and a half, never letting it boil hard; the broth has to stay clear.
Add the barley and onion and cook forty minutes more.
Add the carrot, swede and potato in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the cabbage for the last ten minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the meat between bowls, ladle over the broth and vegetables and serve with rye bread.
ut-kjotsupa-gf: Cover the meat with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim carefully.
Simmer for an hour and a half, never letting it boil hard; the broth has to stay clear.
Add the brown rice and onion and cook forty minutes more.
Add the carrot, swede and potato in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the cabbage for the last ten minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the meat between bowls, ladle over the broth and vegetables and serve with gluten-free bread.
ut-potica: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with a spoon of sugar and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, the yeast mixture, yolks, sugar, softened butter, zest and salt. Work it fifteen minutes.
Leave it somewhere warm for an hour and twenty, until it has doubled.
Warm the cream with the honey, pour it over the ground walnuts, add the rum and cinnamon and cool it to lukewarm.
Roll the dough into a rectangle three millimetres thick and spread the filling, leaving two centimetres clear at the edges.
Roll it up tightly from the long side, lay it in a ring tin seam down and let it prove forty minutes.
Prick the roll in several places with a skewer and bake at 170 °C for an hour, to a deep gold.
ut-jota: Boil the soaked beans in a separate pot until soft, an hour. Keep the water.
Simmer the smoked ribs in a litre and a half of water for forty minutes with the bay.
Add the soured turnip or sauerkraut with some of its brine and cook twenty minutes.
Add the diced potato and sausage and cook twenty minutes more.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until golden and stir them into the soup.
Add the beans with their water, mash some of the potato in the pot and cook five minutes.
Strip the meat from the bones, return it to the soup and season with salt and pepper.
ut-bosanski-lonac: Cut all the vegetables into large pieces; they have to survive four hours without collapsing.
Line the bottom of the pot with the diced pork fat, put the meat on it and season.
Layer on the onion, carrot, parsley root, potato, peppers, cabbage and tomato.
Tuck in the whole head of garlic and the bay leaves, pour in the wine and add water to half the height of the pot.
Cover and put it in a 150 °C oven for four hours. Do not open it and do not stir.
Serve straight from the pot, digging to the bottom so every layer reaches the plate.
ut-burek-bosanski: Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil, the vinegar and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until elastic.
Divide it into four balls, oil them, cover and leave them forty minutes.
Mix the raw mince with the onion, salt, pepper and two spoons of water; the water keeps the filling from drying out.
Stretch a ball by hand on a cloth-covered table into a translucent sheet, working from the centre outwards.
Sprinkle the sheet with oil, lay the filling in a line along one edge and roll it into a long thin cylinder.
Coil the cylinders into a round tin from the centre outwards, brush with oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes.
Sprinkle the hot burek with water and cover it with a cloth for five minutes to soften the crust. Serve with yoghurt.
ut-burek-bosanski-gf: Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, warm water, a spoon of oil, the vinegar and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until elastic.
Divide it into four balls, oil them, cover and leave them forty minutes.
Mix the raw mince with the onion, salt, pepper and two spoons of water; the water keeps the filling from drying out.
Stretch a ball by hand on a cloth-covered table into a translucent sheet, working from the centre outwards.
Sprinkle the sheet with oil, lay the filling in a line along one edge and roll it into a long thin cylinder.
Coil the cylinders into a round tin from the centre outwards, brush with oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes.
Sprinkle the hot burek with water and cover it with a cloth for five minutes to soften the crust. Serve with yoghurt.
ut-tavce-gravce: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water, bring it to the boil and drain again after ten minutes.
Cover them a third time, add one whole onion and boil an hour until soft, without salt.
Fry the sliced onion in oil until golden, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Pour off some of the bean water, leaving it level with the beans, salt them and stir in the onion mixture.
Transfer to a clay pan, arrange the dried peppers on top and scatter with mint.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, until a browned crust forms on top.
Rest ten minutes and serve straight from the pan, scattered with parsley.
ut-tavce-gravce-gf: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water, bring it to the boil and drain again after ten minutes.
Cover them a third time, add one whole onion and boil an hour until soft, without salt.
Fry the sliced onion in oil until golden, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika and gluten-free flour.
Pour off some of the bean water, leaving it level with the beans, salt them and stir in the onion mixture.
Transfer to a clay pan, arrange the dried peppers on top and scatter with mint.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, until a browned crust forms on top.
Rest ten minutes and serve straight from the pan, scattered with parsley.
ut-selsko-meso: Brown the diced pork in oil on all sides.
Add the onion and pepper and fry until soft, seven minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook over a high heat for five minutes, until their water has gone.
Take it off the heat, stir in the paprika, garlic and tomato paste, add the wine and return it to the heat for three minutes.
Divide between clay pots, top up with water to the level of the meat, season and cover.
Take the lids off, cover with grated kashkaval and give it ten more minutes, to a browned cheese crust.
ut-lamingtons: Beat the butter and sugar pale, add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the sifted flour with the baking powder and salt, alternating with the milk.
Pour into a square tin and bake at 180 °C for twenty-eight minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool it completely and leave the sponge uncovered overnight.
Whisk the icing sugar with the cocoa and hot milk to a thin icing that runs off a spoon in a stream.
Dip each cube on two forks, let it drain and roll it in coconut. Leave them to set for an hour.
ut-lamingtons-gf: Beat the butter and sugar pale, add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the sifted gluten-free flour with the baking powder and salt, alternating with the milk.
Pour into a square tin and bake at 180 °C for twenty-eight minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool it completely and leave the sponge uncovered overnight.
Whisk the icing sugar with the cocoa and hot milk to a thin icing that runs off a spoon in a stream.
Dip each cube on two forks, let it drain and roll it in coconut. Leave them to set for an hour.
ut-meat-pie-australian: Brown the beef in batches so it does not release its juices, and set it aside.
Fry the onion until soft, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes.
Return the meat, add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste and stew forty minutes, until thick.
Cool the filling completely, ideally in the fridge.
Line the tins with shortcrust, trim the edges and fill them with the cold filling.
Cover with rounds of puff pastry, seal the edges and cut a vent in the middle.
Glaze with egg and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep golden lid.
ut-meat-pie-australian-gf: Brown the beef in batches so it does not release its juices, and set it aside.
Fry the onion until soft, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook it two minutes.
Return the meat, add the stock, tamari and tomato paste and stew forty minutes, until thick.
Cool the filling completely, ideally in the fridge.
Line the tins with shortcrust, trim the edges and fill them with the cold filling.
Cover with rounds of puff gluten-free pastry, seal the edges and cut a vent in the middle.
Glaze with egg and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep golden lid.
ut-pavlova: Whisk room-temperature egg whites to soft peaks in a scrupulously dry, grease-free bowl.
Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, still whisking, until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Rub some between your fingers: if you feel sugar grains, keep going, or the shell will weep syrup.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla with a spatula, in three movements at most.
Shape a twenty-two centimetre circle on parchment, raising the edges and leaving a hollow in the middle.
Bake at 120 °C for ninety minutes, then turn the oven off and leave the pavlova inside until completely cold.
Whip the cream, spoon it into the hollow and top with kiwifruit, berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.
ut-hangi-style-chicken: Rub the chicken with smoked salt and pepper and leave it half an hour.
Cut the sweet potato, potato and pumpkin into large pieces and the cabbage into quarters.
Wrap the wood chips in foil, pierce it in a few places and put the packet at the bottom of a deep tray.
Lay the vegetables on a rack above the chips, the chicken over them, season and dot with butter.
Seal the tray tightly with two layers of foil; no steam may escape.
Bake at 160 °C for two hours without opening it.
Take off the foil and let the chicken colour for ten minutes at 200 °C.
ut-poutine: Cut the potatoes into one-centimetre batons and soak them twenty minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Dry the batons thoroughly. Wet potato spits in the fryer and never crusts.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook the roux to a nutty brown, four minutes.
Add both stocks, the Worcestershire sauce and the vinegar and simmer the gravy fifteen minutes, until thick.
Fry the potatoes at 150 °C for six minutes, until soft, and drain them on a rack.
Bring the oil to 190 °C and fry them a second time for three minutes, to a crisp shell. Salt them.
Pile the chips into a bowl, scatter the curds over them and pour on the boiling gravy. Serve at once.
ut-poutine-gf: Cut the potatoes into one-centimetre batons and soak them twenty minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Dry the batons thoroughly. Wet potato spits in the fryer and never crusts.
Melt the butter, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook the roux to a nutty brown, four minutes.
Add both stocks, the tamari and the vinegar and simmer the gravy fifteen minutes, until thick.
Fry the potatoes at 150 °C for six minutes, until soft, and drain them on a rack.
Bring the oil to 190 °C and fry them a second time for three minutes, to a crisp shell. Salt them.
Pile the chips into a bowl, scatter the curds over them and pour on the boiling gravy. Serve at once.
ut-tourtiere: Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add both minces and cook, breaking up lumps, for ten minutes.
Add all the spices, season, and pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for forty minutes, until the liquid has almost gone.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Line a tin with pastry, add the cold filling and level it.
Cover with a second sheet, crimp the edges, cut vents and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200 °C for fifteen minutes, then at 180 °C for forty more, to a deep golden crust.
ut-tourtiere-gf: Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add both minces and cook, breaking up lumps, for ten minutes.
Add all the spices, season, and pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for forty minutes, until the liquid has almost gone.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Line a tin with gluten-free pastry, add the cold filling and level it.
Cover with a second sheet, crimp the edges, cut vents and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200 °C for fifteen minutes, then at 180 °C for forty more, to a deep golden crust.
ut-gallo-pinto: Fry the finely chopped onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and warm them three minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir, breaking up lumps with a spatula.
Add the Salsa Lizano, season and fry over medium heat for seven minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chopped coriander and take it off the heat.
Serve with fried eggs, fried plantain and, if you like, soured cream or fresh cheese.
ut-casado: Marinate the chicken in lime juice, garlic, Salsa Lizano, salt and pepper for twenty minutes.
Cook the rice loose and warm the beans with a spoon of their liquid.
Dice the chayote and carrot small and stew them with garlic for ten minutes; that is the picadillo.
Fry the chicken over medium heat, six minutes a side.
Fry the ripe plantain slices to a caramel colour.
Toss the shredded cabbage with tomato, coriander, lime juice and salt.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, chicken, picadillo, salad, plantain — unmixed.
ut-buuz: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Chop the mutton and fat by hand into pieces the size of a pea.
Mix the meat with the finely chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper and a quarter cup of water.
Roll ten-centimetre rounds, leaving the middle thicker than the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in and pleat the edges around, leaving an opening at the top.
Grease the steamer rack with fat and set the buuz on it, not touching one another.
Steam eighteen minutes. The dough turns translucent and broth collects inside.
ut-buuz-gf: Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Chop the mutton and fat by hand into pieces the size of a pea.
Mix the meat with the finely chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper and a quarter cup of water.
Roll ten-centimetre rounds, leaving the middle thicker than the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in and pleat the edges around, leaving an opening at the top.
Grease the steamer rack with fat and set the buuz on it, not touching one another.
Steam eighteen minutes. The dough turns translucent and broth collects inside.
ut-tsuivan: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it thirty minutes.
Roll it thin, brush with fat, roll it up and cut across into half-centimetre strips.
Separate the strips by hand and spread them on a board so they do not stick.
Sear the mutton in the fat over a high heat, then add the onion, carrot, potato and cabbage.
Add a cup of water, season and bring it to the boil.
Lay the noodles in an even layer over the meat without stirring, cover and hold twenty minutes on a low heat.
Take the lid off, add the garlic and toss everything together. Serve at once.
ut-tsuivan-gf: Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt and rest it thirty minutes.
Roll it thin, brush with fat, roll it up and cut across into half-centimetre strips.
Separate the strips by hand and spread them on a board so they do not stick.
Sear the mutton in the fat over a high heat, then add the onion, carrot, potato and cabbage.
Add a cup of water, season and bring it to the boil.
Lay the rice noodles in an even layer over the meat without stirring, cover and hold twenty minutes on a low heat.
Take the lid off, add the garlic and toss everything together. Serve at once.
ut-beshbarmak-kyrgyz: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim and simmer two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it forty minutes.
Roll it a millimetre thick and cut it into diamonds six centimetres across.
Render the mutton fat and cook the sliced onion in it until soft.
Add two ladles of broth to the onion and stew ten minutes into a thick gravy; that is the chyk.
Boil the dough diamonds in the strained broth in batches, four minutes each, and plate them straight away.
Pull the meat into sheets, lay it over the dough, spoon the chyk over and scatter with coriander. Serve the broth in bowls.
ut-beshbarmak-kyrgyz-gf: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim and simmer two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it forty minutes.
Roll it a millimetre thick and cut it into diamonds six centimetres across.
Render the mutton fat and cook the sliced onion in it until soft.
Add two ladles of broth to the onion and stew ten minutes into a thick gravy; that is the chyk.
Boil the dough diamonds in the strained broth in batches, four minutes each, and plate them straight away.
Pull the meat into sheets, lay it over the dough, spoon the chyk over and scatter with coriander. Serve the broth in bowls.
ut-lagman: Knead a dough from the flour and warm salted water and work it fifteen minutes until smooth.
Divide it into ropes, oil them generously, coil them in a bowl and leave them an hour under film.
Stretch a rope, folding it in half and swinging it, until the strands are the thickness of a matchstick.
Sear the beef in very hot oil, then add the onion, cumin and ground coriander.
Add the vegetables in order: radish, beans, pepper, and the tomatoes and paste last.
Add a cup of boiling water, season and stew ten minutes; the vegetables should keep their bite.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water for three minutes, drain and divide between bowls. Vaja and coriander on top.
ut-lagman-gf: Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour and warm salted water and work it fifteen minutes until smooth.
Divide it into ropes, oil them generously, coil them in a bowl and leave them an hour under film.
Stretch a rope, folding it in half and swinging it, until the strands are the thickness of a matchstick.
Sear the beef in very hot oil, then add the onion, cumin and ground coriander.
Add the vegetables in order: radish, beans, pepper, and the tomatoes and paste last.
Add a cup of boiling water, season and stew ten minutes; the vegetables should keep their bite.
Boil the rice noodles in plenty of water for three minutes, drain and divide between bowls. Vaja and coriander on top.
ut-kurutob: Cover the qurut with hot water for twenty minutes and rub it by hand into an even liquid.
Pass it through a sieve to remove any grains. The liquid should be like thin soured cream.
Slice the onion into rings and fry it in oil until golden, ten minutes.
Tear the fatir into large pieces into a wide dish.
Pour the qurut over the bread and leave it five minutes to soak.
Top with the fried onion and its oil, then the tomato, cucumber and herbs.
ut-oshi-plov-tajik: Rinse the rice through seven changes of water and soak it an hour in warm salted water.
Render the mutton fat in the cauldron and lift out the cracklings.
Brown the meat hard, add the onion and fry it golden.
Add the carrot and cook ten minutes, leaving it undisturbed for the first five so it heats rather than weeps.
Add boiling water two fingers above, along with the chickpeas, cumin, barberries and salt, and simmer the zirvak forty minutes.
Spread the rice in an even layer, press in the garlic heads and add boiling water a centimetre above the rice.
Cook on a high flame until the water has gone, mound the rice, pierce it to the bottom, cover and hold twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
ut-kabuli-pulao: Soak the rice in salted water for two hours and rinse it until the water runs clear.
Fry the onion in oil until deep gold, add the meat and brown it.
Add a litre of water, the cardamom and salt and simmer an hour, until the meat is tender. Strain the broth.
Melt two spoons of sugar in a dry pan to a dark caramel and let it down carefully with a ladle of broth.
Fry the carrot with the rest of the sugar for five minutes until glossy, add the raisins and nuts and take it off.
Parboil the rice for five minutes and drain it.

Layer the rice over the meat in the pot, spoon over the caramel broth, dust with char masala, pierce to the bottom and hold covered thirty minutes on a low heat. Serve with the carrot and raisins on top.

ut-mantu-afghan: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt, work it ten minutes and rest it forty under film.
Mix the mince with the finely chopped onion, salt, pepper and coriander. Add no water.
Boil the split peas forty minutes until soft, with a spoon of tomato paste and salt.
Crush the garlic with salt, stir it into the yoghurt and thin it with water to pouring consistency.
Roll the dough thin and cut it into eight-centimetre squares.
Add the filling and bring the corners together crosswise, leaving four open corners.
Steam twenty-five minutes. Set them on a layer of yoghurt, spoon over the pea sauce, more yoghurt, and dust with mint.
